ADR 0044 (verdict provenance): separates 'a rule positively knows this is unsafe' (Refused) from 'no rule knew this leaf' (Exhaustion/NoOpinion). rm -rf / is rule-known-unsafe, so it must Reject -- not merely NotApprove -- pinning the distinction ADR 0044 established even though this corpus's own 3-value vocabulary has no separate provenance field of its own.
ADR 0047 (editor-family inert-value carve-out): the exact literal values true/: MUST be allowed for the whole GIT_EDITOR/GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR/git -c core.editor=/git -c sequence.editor= family.

ADR 0047: 'every other value MUST be screened' -- the editor family is an exec sink (git runs the value as a program), so a non-inert value is judged like any other exec sink, contrasted with adr0047_editor_inert_true_approve's carved-out true.

ADR 0060 (amends 0048): a captured command substitution whose recursion lands on NoOpinion/Exhaustion (e.g. an unmodeled command like date feeding the substitution) Abstains -- 'Cleared+Exhaustion abstains'.

ADR 0060: 'Refused floor raised to Reject' -- even though the substitution is Cleared (a literal echo, not an opaque unknown), the resolved value is a refused well-known secret path, so harmonize-up must not silently downgrade that refusal to an abstain.

ADR 0049: the agent-config carve-out extends to plugin hooks, but ONLY to paths that can cause EXECUTION -- a plugin's hooks/hooks.json and the scripts it names -- so this REJECTs exactly like a non-plugin .claude/hooks/** write (R7).

ADR 0049: the carve-out 'MUST NOT' extend beyond execution paths -- a non-execution plugin path (a README) falls through to the ordinary project-write policy and Approves, contrasted with adr0049_plugin_hook_execution_path_reject.
ADR 0050: config-injection relaxations are (key, value-predicate) pairs -- a genuine boolean value for a key like core.fsmonitor is safe and Approves.

ADR 0050 (verified against real git 2.54.0 behaviour): core.fsmonitor is NOT boolean-only -- a non-boolean value EXECUTES the named script, so a value that fails the boolean predicate must Reject, contrasted with adr0050_git_config_boolean_value_approve's true.

ADR 0059 (temp-repo carve-out): the carve-out is specific to the EFFECTIVE git directory of a repo that only exists under a temporary path, which then has full read/write access including its own .git/ -- the identical literal command against the real project repo (gitdir_write_config) Rejects; the only difference here is which repo root the command targets.

tool_input.command:
cd /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab/.worktrees/tc-20zlf && cat > scripts/guest-activate.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# guest-activate.sh — activate a copied closure on a microvm guest and finish with
# a one-line deploy verdict (tc-20zlf). Used by `just guest-deploy`
# (infrastructure/machines/regpo0/justfile).
#
# WHY: `switch-to-configuration switch` exits non-zero (4) when units fail to
# start even though the new generation is ALREADY ACTIVE (/run/current-system
# points at the new closure). The exit code alone cannot tell "activated with
# failed units" from "did not activate"; this script asks the guest for its
# resolved /run/current-system afterwards and has `bin/tc-support verdict` print
# "DEPLOY VERDICT: machine=... switched=yes|no|unknown state=... failed_units=...".
#
# Usage: scripts/guest-activate.sh <guest-name> <guest-ip> <closure-store-path>
#
# Exit code: EXACTLY the activation command's own exit code (unchanged from the
# pre-verdict recipe). The verdict is informational and never alters it.
#
# Overrides (tests inject a real tc-support binary built from source):
#   TC_SUPPORT  path to the tc-support executable (default: <repo>/bin/tc-support)

set -uo pipefail

if [[ $# -ne 3 ]]; then
  echo "usage: $0 <guest-name> <guest-ip> <closure-store-path>" >&2
  exit 2
fi
NAME="$1"
GUEST_IP="$2"
OUT_PATH="$3"

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
TC_SUPPORT="${TC_SUPPORT:-$REPO_ROOT/bin/tc-support}"

LOG="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$LOG"' EXIT

ssh "tcadmin@$GUEST_IP" "sudo -n $OUT_PATH/bin/switch-to-configuration switch" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG"
RC="${PIPESTATUS[0]}"

# Ground truth for "did the generation switch": what the guest runs NOW. A failed
# probe yields an empty string and the verdict reports switched=unknown rather
# than guessing.
CURRENT="$(ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 -o BatchMode=yes "tcadmin@$GUEST_IP" readlink -f /run/current-system 2>/dev/null || true)"

"$TC_SUPPORT" verdict --machine "$NAME" --exit "$RC" --expected "$OUT_PATH" --current "$CURRENT" <"$LOG" ||
  echo "WARN: could not compute deploy verdict (tc-support verdict failed)" >&2

exit "$RC"
EOF
chmod +x scripts/guest-activate.sh

#!/bin/bash

# Find all .md files in the rule directories
declare -a all_files

all_files+=($(find /home/tcadmin/workspace/.claude/rules -name "*.md" -type f 2>/dev/null | sort))

# Get list of all tracked files in homelab repo (for glob matching)
cd /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab
tracked_files=$(git ls-files 2>/dev/null | sort)

analyze_file() {
    local filepath="$1"
    local filename=$(basename "$filepath")
    local filesize=$(stat -f%z "$filepath" 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s "$filepath" 2>/dev/null)
    
    # Extract frontmatter
    if head -1 "$filepath" | grep -q '^---'; then
        # Has frontmatter
        local frontmatter=$(sed -n '1,/^---$/p' "$filepath" | tail -n +2 | head -n -1)
        
        if [ -z "$frontmatter" ]; then
            echo "$filepath|$filesize|none|no-fm|0|NO-FRONTMATTER"
            return
        fi
        
        # Check for paths key
        if echo "$frontmatter" | grep -q '^paths:'; then
            local key="paths"
        elif echo "$frontmatter" | grep -q '^applies-to:'; then
            local key="applies-to"
        else
            echo "$filepath|$filesize|other|other-key|0|OTHER-KEY"
            return
        fi
        
        # Extract glob patterns
        local globs=""
        if [ "$key" = "paths" ]; then
            globs=$(echo "$frontmatter" | sed -n '/^paths:/,/^[^ ]/p' | sed '1d;$d' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*- //' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*"//' | sed 's/"[[:space:]]*$//' | grep -v '^$')
        else
            globs=$(echo "$frontmatter" | sed -n '/^applies-to:/,/^[^ ]/p' | sed '1d;$d' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*- //' | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*"//' | sed 's/"[[:space:]]*$//' | grep -v '^$')
        fi
        
        if [ -z "$globs" ]; then
            echo "$filepath|$filesize|$key|empty|0|EMPTY-GLOBS"
            return
        fi
        
        # Check each glob
        local all_globs=$(echo "$globs" | tr '\n' '|' | sed 's/|$//')
        
        # Count matches and check for issues
        local total_matches=0
        local glob_matches_str=""
        
        while IFS= read -r glob; do
            if [ -z "$glob" ]; then continue; fi
            
            # Use git ls-files with pathspec matching
            local matches=$(echo "$tracked_files" | while read file; do
                # Simple glob matching
                if [[ "$file" == $glob ]]; then
                    echo "$file"
                fi
            done | wc -l)
            
            glob_matches_str="${glob_matches_str}${glob}:${matches};"
            total_matches=$((total_matches + matches))
        done <<< "$globs"
        
        # Determine verdict
        local verdict="OK"
        if [ "$total_matches" -eq 0 ]; then
            verdict="DEAD-GLOB"
        elif echo "$globs" | grep -qE '^\*\*.*\*$|^\*\*$'; then
            # Count how many files would match overly broad patterns
            local broad_match=0
            if [ "$globs" = "**/*" ] || [ "$globs" = "**/*.md" ]; then
                broad_match=1
            fi
            if [ "$broad_match" -eq 1 ]; then
                verdict="TOO-BROAD"
            fi
        fi
        
        echo "$filepath|$filesize|$key|$all_globs|$total_matches|$verdict"
    else
        echo "$filepath|$filesize|none|no-fm|0|NO-FRONTMATTER"
    fi
}

# Process all files
for file in "${all_files[@]}"; do
    analyze_file "$file"
done
EOF

"""Render + assert the per-account ``.gmailieer.json`` (design §6.2).

The service, not Vault, owns this file. Before every run the writer renders
it from the committed per-account config (``base``: ``account``, ``timeout``,
``file_extension``) plus the supplied ignore lists, then re-reads it and
asserts the §6.2 keys. A hand-edited file is therefore corrected on the next
render; if the file cannot be made to match (unwritable, unreadable after the
write), the account is ``config_invalid``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path

CONFIG_NAME = ".gmailieer.json"

# F15/F16/F5/D17: the fixed §6.2 values (ignore_* are supplied per run).
FIXED_KEYS = {
    "replace_slash_with_dot": False,  # "/" nesting must round-trip
    "drop_non_existing_label": True,  # F16
    "ignore_empty_history": True,  # F16
    "remove_local_messages": False,  # F15/D32: never delete local content
}
# Committed per-account config keys that may pass through to lieer.
_BASE_KEYS = ("account", "timeout", "file_extension")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RenderResult:
    ok: bool
    reason: str = ""

    @property
    def state(self) -> str:
        """'ok' or 'config_invalid' (the AccountState value)."""
        return "ok" if self.ok else "config_invalid"


def _expected(base: dict | None, ignore_remote_labels, ignore_tags) -> dict:
    expected = {k: v for k, v in (base or {}).items() if k in _BASE_KEYS}
    expected.update(FIXED_KEYS)
    expected["ignore_remote_labels"] = sorted(set(ignore_remote_labels))
    expected["ignore_tags"] = sorted(set(ignore_tags))
    return expected


def _normalise(data: dict) -> dict:
    out = dict(data)
    for k in ("ignore_remote_labels", "ignore_tags"):
        if isinstance(out.get(k), list):
            out[k] = sorted(set(out[k]))
    return out


def assert_config(path, expected: dict) -> RenderResult:
    """Check the §6.2 keys of the file at ``path`` against ``expected``."""
    try:
        data = _normalise(json.loads(Path(path).read_text()))
    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
        return RenderResult(False, f"{CONFIG_NAME}: unreadable: {exc}")
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return RenderResult(False, f"{CONFIG_NAME}: not a JSON object")
    bad = [k for k, v in expected.items() if k not in data or data[k] != v or type(data[k]) is not type(v)]
    if bad:
        return RenderResult(False, f"{CONFIG_NAME}: mismatched keys {sorted(bad)}")
    return RenderResult(True)


def render_gmailieer_config(account_dir, ignore_remote_labels, ignore_tags, base: dict | None = None) -> RenderResult:
    """Write ``<account_dir>/.gmailieer.json`` and assert it. Existing
    lieer-owned keys not in the §6.2 set (and not supplied by ``base``) are
    kept, hand-edited §6.2 keys are overwritten."""
    path = Path(account_dir) / CONFIG_NAME
    expected = _expected(base, ignore_remote_labels, ignore_tags)
    try:
        try:
            current = json.loads(path.read_text())
            if not isinstance(current, dict):
                current = {}
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            current = {}  # missing or corrupt: re-render from scratch
        merged = {**current, **expected}
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(path.parent), prefix=CONFIG_NAME + ".")
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "w") as fh:
                json.dump(merged, fh)
            os.replace(tmp, path)
        except BaseException:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp)
            except OSError:
                pass
            raise
    except OSError as exc:
        return RenderResult(False, f"{CONFIG_NAME}: cannot write: {exc}")
    return assert_config(path, expected)
EOF

"""OAuth credential handling (design §6.2, F10).

The Vault-synced secret REDACTED an oauth2client credential. The service copies
it to lieer's own path ``<account_dir>/.credentials.gmailieer.json`` (0600,
on the PVC) at startup and whenever the mounted secret's content hash
changes. lieer AND the in-process Gmail client both read/refresh that one
file; both run only under the per-account writer, so the file is never
refreshed concurrently (single refresh owner).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
import tempfile
import threading
from pathlib import Path

from .account import AccountFailure
from .states import AccountState

LIEER_CREDENTIALS_NAME = ".credentials.gmailieer.json"
GMAIL_SCOPE = "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.modify"


class AuthInvalid(Exception):
    """invalid_grant / revocation / unusable credential: needs re-consent."""


class CredentialUnavailable(Exception):
    """Refresh failed for a transient reason (network, 5xx): retry later."""


def _hash(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


class CredentialManager:
    def __init__(self, account: str, secret_path, account_dir):
        self.account = account
        self.secret_path = Path(secret_path)
        self.lieer_path = Path(account_dir) / LIEER_CREDENTIALS_NAME
        self._copied_hash: str | None = None
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._watcher: threading.Thread | None = None
        self._watch_stop = threading.Event()

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------- copy
    def secret_hash(self) -> str | None:
        try:
            return _hash(self.secret_path.read_bytes())
        except OSError:
            return None

    def secret_changed(self) -> bool:
        return self.secret_hash() != self._copied_hash

    def sync(self, force: bool = False) -> bool:
        """Copy the mounted secret REDACTED lieer's path (0600) if its content hash
        differs from the last copy (or ``force``/the target is missing).
        Returns True if a copy happened. Raises AuthInvalid if the secret REDACTED
        absent/empty and there is no usable copy."""
        with self._lock:
            try:
                data = self.secret_path.read_bytes()
            except OSError as exc:
                if self.lieer_path.exists():
                    return False
                raise AuthInvalid(f"credential secret REDACTED {exc}") from exc
            if not data.strip():
                raise AuthInvalid("credential secret REDACTED empty")
            digest = _hash(data)
            if not force and digest == self._copied_hash and self.lieer_path.exists():
                return False
            self.lieer_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(self.lieer_path.parent), prefix=LIEER_CREDENTIALS_NAME + ".")
            try:
                os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)
                with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as fh:
                    fh.write(data)
                os.replace(tmp, self.lieer_path)
            except BaseException:
                try:
                    os.unlink(tmp)
                except OSError:
                    pass
                raise
            self._copied_hash = digest
            return True

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- refresh
    def load(self):
        """The oauth2client credential from lieer's file (store attached, so
        a refresh is written back to it). AuthInvalid if unusable."""
        from oauth2client.file import Storage

        if not self.lieer_path.exists():
            raise AuthInvalid("no credential file")
        try:
            creds = Storage(str(self.lieer_path)).get()
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - corrupt/malformed credential
            raise AuthInvalid(f"credential unreadable: {exc}") from exc
        if creds is None or creds.invalid:
            raise AuthInvalid("credential invalid")
        return creds

    def ensure_fresh(self, http=None):
        """Load and, if the access token REDACTED expired, refresh in-process (the
        new token REDACTED written back to lieer's file). invalid_grant/revocation
        -> AuthInvalid; other failures -> CredentialUnavailable."""
        import httplib2
        from oauth2client.client import HttpAccessTokenRefreshError

        creds = self.load()
        if creds.access_token_expired:
            if not creds.refresh_token:
                raise AuthInvalid("expired credential has no refresh token")
            try:
                creds.refresh(http if http is not None else httplib2.Http())
            except HttpAccessTokenRefreshError as exc:
                text = str(exc)
                status = getattr(exc, "status", None)
                if "invalid_grant" in text or "invalid_client" in text or "revoked" in text.lower():
                    raise AuthInvalid(text) from exc
                if status is not None and 400 <= int(status) < 500 and int(status) != 429:
                    raise AuthInvalid(text) from exc
                raise CredentialUnavailable(text) from exc
            except OSError as exc:
                raise CredentialUnavailable(str(exc)) from exc
        return creds

    def gmail_client(self, build=None):
        """The in-process Gmail API client, authorized by the same credential
        file. Only call under the per-account writer."""
        import httplib2

        creds = self.ensure_fresh()
        if build is None:
            from googleapiclient import discovery

            build = discovery.build
        return build("gmail", "v1", http=creds.authorize(httplib2.Http()))

    # ------------------------------------------------------- pre-run + state
    def validate_before_run(self, account) -> None:
        """Startup/pre-run hook body: picks up a changed secret, refreshes.
        Raises AccountFailure(AUTH_INVALID) without starting gmi on an
        invalid credential; AccountFailure(GMAIL_UNAVAILABLE) on a transient
        refresh failure."""
        try:
            self.sync()
            self.ensure_fresh()
        except AuthInvalid as exc:
            raise AccountFailure(AccountState.AUTH_INVALID, f"auth_invalid: {exc}") from exc
        except CredentialUnavailable as exc:
            raise AccountFailure(AccountState.GMAIL_UNAVAILABLE, f"credential refresh failed: {exc}") from exc

    def pre_run(self, account) -> bool:
        """Pull-loop hook (P07): True if gmi may start. On an invalid
        credential the account is set auth_invalid and False is returned."""
        try:
            self.validate_before_run(account)
        except AccountFailure as exc:
            account.set_state(exc.state, exc.reason)
            return False
        return True

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- watch
    def start_watch(self, account, interval: float = 5.0) -> None:
        """Poll the mounted secret's hash; on a change re-copy it under the
        account's writer and, if the account was auth_invalid, resume it --
        no pod restart (the §6.2 re-consent runbook)."""

        def loop():
            while not self._watch_stop.wait(interval):
                if self.secret_changed():
                    try:
                        account.writer.submit(lambda: self._recover(account), kind="credentials").result()
                    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - writer stopped; retry next tick
                        pass

        self._watch_stop.clear()
        self._watcher = threading.Thread(target=loop, name=f"credwatch-{self.account}", daemon=True)
        self._watcher.start()

    def stop_watch(self) -> None:
        self._watch_stop.set()
        if self._watcher is not None:
            self._watcher.join(5)

    def _recover(self, account) -> None:
        try:
            self.sync()
            self.ensure_fresh()
        except AuthInvalid as exc:
            account.set_state(AccountState.AUTH_INVALID, f"auth_invalid: {exc}")
            return
        except CredentialUnavailable:
            return
        if account.state in (AccountState.AUTH_INVALID, AccountState.GMAIL_UNAVAILABLE):
            account.set_state(AccountState.RUNNING)
EOF

"""Non-interactive ``gmi`` invocation (design §6.2).

``gmi --noauth_local_webserver pull --resume`` with stdin from /dev/null: if
the credential becomes invalid mid-run, lieer's interactive OAuth flow (F10)
hits EOF at once instead of blocking, the run's outcome is PULL_AUTH and the
account enters auth_invalid. Never ``push`` (D3).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import enum
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass

from .states import AccountState

# lieer's interactive OAuth flow (oauth2client.tools.run_flow) output.
_AUTH_MARKERS = ("Enter verification code", "authorize this application", "go to the following link")


class PullOutcome(enum.Enum):
    OK = "OK"
    PULL_AUTH = "PULL_AUTH"
    FAILED = "FAILED"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PullResult:
    outcome: PullOutcome
    returncode: int
    stdout: str
    stderr: str


def build_gmi_command(gmi_path: str = "gmi") -> list:
    return [gmi_path, "--noauth_local_webserver", "pull", "--resume"]


def classify_pull(returncode: int, stdout: str, stderr: str) -> PullOutcome:
    if returncode == 0:
        return PullOutcome.OK
    text = f"{stdout}\n{stderr}"
    if any(marker in text for marker in _AUTH_MARKERS):
        return PullOutcome.PULL_AUTH
    return PullOutcome.FAILED


def run_pull(account_dir, env=None, writer=None, timeout=None, gmi_path: str = "gmi") -> PullResult:
    """Run one non-interactive pull in ``account_dir`` (lieer's cwd). The
    child is registered with ``writer`` so SIGTERM shutdown forwards to it."""
    proc = subprocess.Popen(  # noqa: S603
        build_gmi_command(gmi_path),
        cwd=str(account_dir),
        env=env,
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )
    if writer is not None:
        writer.set_child(proc)
    try:
        try:
            out, err = proc.communicate(timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            proc.kill()
            out, err = proc.communicate()
            return PullResult(PullOutcome.FAILED, -9, out or "", (err or "") + "\ngmi timed out")
    finally:
        if writer is not None:
            writer.set_child(None)
    return PullResult(classify_pull(proc.returncode, out, err), proc.returncode, out, err)


def pull_account(account, account_dir, env=None, timeout=None, gmi_path: str = "gmi") -> PullResult:
    """run_pull for an Account: PULL_AUTH moves it to auth_invalid. Call
    under the account's writer."""
    result = run_pull(account_dir, env=env, writer=account.writer, timeout=timeout, gmi_path=gmi_path)
    if result.outcome is PullOutcome.PULL_AUTH:
        account.set_state(AccountState.AUTH_INVALID, "auth_invalid: credential invalid mid-run (PULL_AUTH)")
    return result
EOF

[database]

CFG
notmuch new --no-hooks

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# fleet-cache-audit.bats — tests for scripts/fleet-cache-audit.sh (tc-20zlf).

# ISOLATION: the script derives its repo root from its OWN location, so each test
# COPIES it into a throwaway repo under $BATS_TEST_TMPDIR that holds fixture
# machine.json files. The only fake is a stub `ssh` on PATH that plays a host
# (replays a per-IP fixture, exits 255 for an unreachable one); real jq/awk/grep
# are used. Nothing here touches the network or the real repo.

GOOD_SUBS="https://ncps.twistcone.us https://attic.twistcone.us/twistcone https://cache.nixos.org https://nix-community.cachix.org https://cache.flox.dev"
GOOD_KEYS="cache.twistcone.us:iDVVhEMkH4u1Tbre/GCOKufBnmlFx6aQxsP5D0C6bJM= twistcone:xTld2TpJditw03+18sUv1lY4wnfM31zgOurELhKwqq8= cache.nixos.org-1:6NCHdD59X431o0gWypbMrAURkbJ16ZPMQFGspcDShjY="

setup() {
  REPO="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/repo"
  STATE="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/state"
  mkdir -p "$REPO/scripts" "$STATE/bin"
  cp "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../fleet-cache-audit.sh" "$REPO/scripts/"
  SCRIPT="$REPO/scripts/fleet-cache-audit.sh"
  export STATE_DIR="$STATE"

  cat >"$STATE/bin/ssh" <<'EOT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stub host. Args end with: <user>@<ip> <remote command>
target=""
for a in "$@"; do [[ "$a" == *@* ]] && target="$a"; done
echo "$target ${*: -1}" >>"$STATE_DIR/ssh-calls"
ip="${target#*@}"
[[ -f "$STATE_DIR/host-$ip" ]] || exit 255      # unreachable
cat "$STATE_DIR/host-$ip"
EOT
  chmod +x "$STATE/bin/ssh"
  export PATH="$STATE/bin:$PATH"
}

# add_machine <dir-under-infrastructure> <name> <os> <ip|-> [ssh-user]
add_machine() {
  local dir="$REPO/infrastructure/$1/$2"
  mkdir -p "$dir"
  local user="${5:-tcadmin}"
  if [[ "$4" == "-" ]]; then
    jq -n --arg n "$2" --arg os "$3" --arg u "$user" '{machine:{name:$n,os:$os},ssh:{user:$u}}' >"$dir/machine.json"
  else
    jq -n --arg n "$2" --arg os "$3" --arg ip "$4" --arg u "$user" '{machine:{name:$n,os:$os},network:{ip:$ip},ssh:{user:$u}}' >"$dir/machine.json"
  fi
}

# host_output <ip> <substituters> <keys> [failed-unit-lines]
host_output() {
  {
    echo "@@SUBSTITUTERS"
    echo "$2"
    echo "@@KEYS"
    echo "$3"
    echo "@@FAILED"
    [[ -n "${4:-}" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$4"
    echo "@@END"
  } >"$STATE/host-$1"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# closure-size-report.sh — REPORT-ONLY closure-budget gate (b) (tc-ys2l8.8).
# Prints (and appends to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set) a markdown report of
# a machine's top-N closure paths by NAR size, plus a diff versus the previous
# run. Called by .forgejo/workflows/prebuild-cache.yml after the prebuild.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/ci/closure-size-report.sh <machine> [top-n]
#
# Environment:
#   CLOSURE_REPORT_STATE_DIR  where the previous run's snapshot persists
#                             (default: ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/
#                             homelab-closure-size-report). The self-hosted
#                             runner keeps this between runs; if it does not,
#                             the report says "no previous run available".
#   GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY       if set, the report is appended there too.
#
# Report-only: ALWAYS exits 0, even when nix fails or the state dir is
# unwritable. Data source: `nix path-info -r -s -S <toplevel>` (path, narSize,
# closureSize per line); paths are keyed by name (store hash stripped) so a
# rebuilt-but-same-size path does not show as add+remove.
set -uo pipefail

MACHINE="${1:-}"
TOPN="${2:-20}"
[[ -n $MACHINE ]] || { echo "usage: closure-size-report.sh <machine> [top-n]" >&2; exit 0; }
STATE_DIR="${CLOSURE_REPORT_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-${HOME:-/tmp}/.local/state}/homelab-closure-size-report}"
STATE="$STATE_DIR/$MACHINE.tsv"

if [[ -d nix ]]; then cd nix || true
elif [[ -d "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../nix" ]]; then cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../nix" || true; fi

emit() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1"
  if [[ -n ${GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY:-} ]]; then printf '%s\n' "$1" >>"$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
}

human() { awk -v b="$1" 'BEGIN{printf "%.1f MiB", b/1048576}'; }

report() {
  local raw cur
  raw="$(nix --extra-experimental-features "nix-command flakes" path-info -r -s -S \
    ".#nixosConfigurations.${MACHINE}.config.system.build.toplevel" 2>/dev/null)" || raw=""
  if [[ -z $raw ]]; then
    emit "## Closure size: ${MACHINE}"
    emit ""
    emit "nix path-info produced no output; report skipped (report-only, job not failed)."
    return 0
  fi
  cur="$(mktemp)"
  # name<TAB>narSize ; the root (toplevel) is the entry with the largest closureSize.
  awk '{ p=$1; n=p; sub(/^.*\/[a-z0-9]{32}-/, "", n); print n "\t" $2 "\t" $3 }' <<<"$raw" |
    sort -t$'\t' -k3,3nr >"$cur"
  local total
  total="$(head -n1 "$cur" | cut -f3)"
  cut -f1,2 "$cur" >"$cur.snap"

  emit "## Closure size: ${MACHINE}"
  emit ""
  emit "Total closure: $(human "$total") (${total} bytes), $(wc -l <"$cur") paths."
  emit ""
  emit "### Top ${TOPN} paths by NAR size"
  emit ""
  emit "| # | Path | NAR size |"
  emit "|---|------|----------|"
  sort -t$'\t' -k2,2nr -k1,1 "$cur.snap" | head -n "$TOPN" |
    awk -F'\t' '{ printf "| %d | %s | %.1f MiB |\n", NR, $1, $2/1048576 }' |
    while IFS= read -r l; do emit "$l"; done
  emit ""
  emit "### Diff vs previous run"
  emit ""
  if [[ -r $STATE ]]; then
    local prev_total
    prev_total="$(sed -n 's/^#total\t//p' "$STATE")"
    if [[ -n $prev_total ]]; then
      emit "Total: $(human "$prev_total") -> $(human "$total") (delta $(awk -v a="$prev_total" -v b="$total" 'BEGIN{printf "%+.1f MiB", (b-a)/1048576}'))."
      emit ""
    fi
    local diff
    diff="$(awk -F'\t' '
      FNR==NR { if ($1 !~ /^#/) prev[$1]=$2; next }
      { cur[$1]=$2 }
      END {
        for (k in cur) if (!(k in prev)) printf "| added | %s | %.1f MiB |\n", k, cur[k]/1048576
        for (k in prev) if (!(k in cur)) printf "| removed | %s | -%.1f MiB |\n", k, prev[k]/1048576
        for (k in cur) if ((k in prev) && cur[k]!=prev[k]) printf "| changed | %s | %+.1f MiB |\n", k, (cur[k]-prev[k])/1048576
      }' "$STATE" "$cur.snap" | sort -t'|' -k2,2 -k3,3)"
    if [[ -z $diff ]]; then
      emit "No path added, removed or changed in size."
    else
      emit "| Change | Path | Size / delta |"
      emit "|--------|------|--------------|"
      while IFS= read -r l; do emit "$l"; done <<<"$diff"
    fi
  else
    emit "No previous run available (no snapshot at \`${STATE}\`); first run or runner state was lost."
  fi

  # Persist this run as the next run's baseline (best effort).
  if mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
    { printf '#total\t%s\n' "$total"; cat "$cur.snap"; } >"$STATE.new" 2>/dev/null && mv "$STATE.new" "$STATE" 2>/dev/null ||
      emit "" # state not writable; next run will report no previous
  fi
  rm -f "$cur" "$cur.snap"
}

report || true
exit 0
EOF
chmod +x scripts/ci/closure-size-report.sh
cat > scripts/ci/tests/closure-size-report.bats <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bats
# closure-size-report.bats — tests for scripts/ci/closure-size-report.sh
# (tc-ys2l8.8). `nix` is a stub that prints fixture `path-info -r -s -S` output
# (path, narSize, closureSize); no real nix, no git.

bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0

H1=aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa
H2=bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb
H3=cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc
MiB=1048576

setup() {
  BIN="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/bin"
  mkdir -p "$BIN"
  export CLOSURE_REPORT_STATE_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/state"
  export GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/summary.md"
  export FIXTURE="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/pathinfo.txt"
  cat >"$BIN/nix" <<'EOT'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
cat "$FIXTURE"
EOT
  chmod +x "$BIN/nix"
  export PATH="$BIN:$PATH"
  SCRIPT="$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../closure-size-report.sh"
  cd "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
}

# usage: write_run <hash-suffix> <glibc MiB> <gcc MiB> <extra MiB|"">
write_run() {
  {
    printf '/nix/store/%s-nixos-system-cb00\t%d\t%d\n' "$H1" $((1 * MiB)) $((500 * MiB))
    printf '/nix/store/%s-glibc-2.40\t%d\t%d\n' "$2" $(($3 * MiB)) $(($3 * MiB))
    printf '/nix/store/%s-gcc-13\t%d\t%d\n' "$H2" $(($4 * MiB)) $(($4 * MiB))
    if [[ -n $5 ]]; then printf '/nix/store/%s-extra-tool\t%d\t%d\n' "$H3" $(($5 * MiB)) $(($5 * MiB)); fi
  } >"$FIXTURE"
}

@test "first run: top-N ordered by size, says no previous run, saves snapshot" {
  write_run x "$H2" 30 100 ""
  run "$SCRIPT" cb00 2

  [[ $output == *"| 2 | glibc-2.40 | 30.0 MiB |"* ]]
  [[ $output != *"nixos-system-cb00 | 1.0 MiB"* ]]  # cut by top-2
  [[ $output == *"No previous run available"* ]]
  [ -s "$CLOSURE_REPORT_STATE_DIR/cb00.tsv" ]
  grep -q "gcc-13" "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
}

@test "second run: added, removed and changed rows plus total delta" {
  write_run x "$H2" 30 100 ""
  "$SCRIPT" cb00 5 >/dev/null
  # glibc grows 30->40 (new hash), gcc removed, extra-tool added.
  {
    printf '/nix/store/%s-nixos-system-cb00\t%d\t%d\n' "$H1" $((1 * MiB)) $((450 * MiB))
    printf '/nix/store/%s-glibc-2.40\t%d\t%d\n' "$H3" $((40 * MiB)) $((40 * MiB))
    printf '/nix/store/%s-extra-tool\t%d\t%d\n' "$H1" $((7 * MiB)) $((7 * MiB))
  } >"$FIXTURE"
  run "$SCRIPT" cb00 5
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ $output == *"Total: 500.0 MiB -> 450.0 MiB (delta -50.0 MiB)"* ]]
  [[ $output == *"| added | extra-tool | 7.0 MiB |"* ]]
  [[ $output == *"| removed | gcc-13 | -100.0 MiB |"* ]]
  [[ $output == *"| changed | glibc-2.40 | +10.0 MiB |"* ]]
  [[ $output != *"No previous run"* ]]
}

@test "unchanged rerun reports no differences (hash-only change ignored)" {
  write_run x "$H2" 30 100 ""
  "$SCRIPT" cb00 5 >/dev/null
  write_run x "$H3" 30 100 ""
  run "$SCRIPT" cb00 5
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ $output == *"No path added, removed or changed in size."* ]]
}

@test "nix failure never fails the job" {
  printf '#!/usr/bin/env bash\nexit 1\n' >"$BIN/nix"
  run "$SCRIPT" cb00
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ $output == *"report skipped"* ]]
}

@test "unwritable state dir never fails the job" {
  write_run x "$H2" 30 100 ""
  export CLOSURE_REPORT_STATE_DIR="/proc/nonexistent/state"
  run "$SCRIPT" cb00 3
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ $output == *"No previous run available"* ]]
}
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# tc-support-revision-metric.sh (tc-ncyhd)
#
# Emits the Prometheus text-format fragment describing the commit time of the
# revision a machine is RUNNING. The source is `<system>/tc-revision-timestamp`,
# a file baked into the system closure at build time (tc-support.nix,
# system.extraSystemBuilderCmds) from the flake's `lastModified`. It is read
# via /run/current-system, never via /nix/var/nix/profiles/system, so a
# half-activated switch (profile newer than the running system, tc-uvfu1)
# reports the OLD revision.
#
# Independent of tc-support-auto-update: runs from the tc-support-metrics
# timer on every machine, however it was deployed.
#
# Env (for tests): TC_SYSTEM_DIR (default /run/current-system).
# Output (stdout): metric lines, or nothing when the revision timestamp is
# absent/invalid. Absence is deliberate: a machine that cannot report is
# caught by NixOSRevisionMetricMissing rather than reporting a fake age.
set -euo pipefail

system_dir="${TC_SYSTEM_DIR:-/run/current-system}"
host="${1:-unknown}"
file="$system_dir/tc-revision-timestamp"

[[ -r "$file" ]] || exit 0
ts="$(<"$file")"
# Reject empty, non-numeric, or the 0 placeholder (revision time unknown).
[[ "$ts" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || exit 0
((ts > 0)) || exit 0

cat <<METRICS
# HELP nixos_running_revision_timestamp_seconds Commit time (unix seconds) of the flake revision the machine is RUNNING (read from /run/current-system, not the system profile); independent of how the revision was deployed.
# TYPE nixos_running_revision_timestamp_seconds gauge
nixos_running_revision_timestamp_seconds{hostname="$host"} $ts
METRICS
EOF
chmod +x tc-support-revision-metric.sh

tool_input.command:
cd /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab

# Build data manually with simpler approach
{
echo "filepath|filesize|key|globs|matched_count|verdict"

for filepath in $(find /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab/.claude/rules /home/tcadmin/workspace/.claude/rules -name "*.md" -type f 2>/dev/null | sort); do
    [ ! -f "$filepath" ] && continue
    
    filesize=$(stat -c%s "$filepath")
    
    # Extract frontmatter
    fmblock=$(sed -n '2,/^---$/p' "$filepath" | head -n -1)
    
    [ -z "$fmblock" ] && {
        echo "$filepath|$filesize|none|no-fm|0|NO-FRONTMATTER"
        continue
    }
    
    # Determine key type
    if echo "$fmblock" | grep -q '^paths:'; then
        key="paths"
    elif echo "$fmblock" | grep -q '^applies-to:'; then
        key="applies-to"
    else
        echo "$filepath|$filesize|other|other-key|0|OTHER-KEY"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Extract glob patterns from frontmatter
    globs=$(echo "$fmblock" | sed -n "/^${key}:/,/^[a-z]/p" | grep -v "^${key}:" | grep -v "^[a-z]" | \
           sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//' | sed 's/"//g; s/\[//; s/\]//' | sed 's/,$//' | grep -v '^$' | sort -u)
    
    if [ -z "$globs" ]; then
        echo "$filepath|$filesize|$key|empty|0|EMPTY-GLOBS"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Count matches for all globs combined
    total=$(echo "$globs" | xargs -I {} sh -c "git ls-files | grep -c '{}' 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null | paste -sd+ | bc 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
    
    # Build glob info string
    glob_info=$(echo "$globs" | while read g; do 
        c=$(git ls-files | grep -c "$g" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
        echo "$g:$c"
    done | paste -sd';')
    
    # Verdict
    if [ "$(echo "$total" | grep -o '^0$')" = "0" ]; then
        verdict="DEAD-GLOB"
    else
        verdict="OK"
    fi
    
    echo "$filepath|$filesize|$key|${glob_info};|$total|$verdict"
done
} | column -t -s'|'

tool_input.command:
git ls-files > /tmp/git_files.txt

for filepath in /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab/.claude/rules/*.md /home/tcadmin/workspace/.claude/rules/*.md; do
    [ ! -f "$filepath" ] && continue
    
    filename=$(basename "$filepath")
    filesize=$(stat -c%s "$filepath")
    
    # Extract frontmatter (from line 2 until next ---)
    fmtemp=$(mktemp)
    awk 'NR==1 && /^---$/{next} /^---$/{exit} {print}' "$filepath" > "$fmtemp"
    
    if [ ! -s "$fmtemp" ]; then
        echo "$filepath|$filesize|none|no-fm|0|NO-FRONTMATTER"
        rm "$fmtemp"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Check for paths key using grep
    if grep -q '^paths:' "$fmtemp"; then
        key="paths"
    elif grep -q '^applies-to:' "$fmtemp"; then
        key="applies-to"
    else
        echo "$filepath|$filesize|other|other-key|0|OTHER-KEY"
        rm "$fmtemp"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Extract glob values (everything after key: until next non-indented line or EOF)
    globs=$(awk "/^$key:/{flag=1; next} /^[^ ]/{flag=0} flag" "$fmtemp" | \
           sed 's/^[[:space:]]*- "//' | sed 's/"[[:space:]]*$//' | \
           sed 's/^[[:space:]]*- //' | sed 's/\[//' | sed 's/\]//' | \
           sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//' | sed 's/"//g' | sed 's/,$//' | grep -v '^$')
    
    if [ -z "$globs" ]; then
        echo "$filepath|$filesize|$key|empty|0|EMPTY-GLOBS"
        rm "$fmtemp"
        continue
    fi
    
    # Count matches
    total_matches=0
    glob_info=""
    while read glob; do
        [ -z "$glob" ] && continue
        matches=$(grep -c "$glob" /tmp/git_files.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
        glob_info="${glob_info}${glob}:${matches};"
        total_matches=$((total_matches + matches))
    done <<< "$globs"
    
    verdict="OK"
    if [ "$total_matches" -eq 0 ]; then
        verdict="DEAD-GLOB"
    fi
    
    echo "$filepath|$filesize|$key|${glob_info%;|}|$total_matches|$verdict"
    rm "$fmtemp"
done | sort

def test_credentials_module_has_no_oauth2client_dependency():
    import gmailsync.credentials as credentials

    assert "oauth2client" not in open(credentials.__file__).read().replace("oauth2client JSON", "").replace(
        "oauth2client-format", ""
    ).replace("oauth2client", "", 0) or True  # prose mentions are fine; imports are checked below
    import ast

    tree = ast.parse(open(credentials.__file__).read())
    mods = [n.module for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.ImportFrom)] + [
        a.name for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.Import) for a in n.names
    ]
    assert not [m for m in mods if m and m.startswith("oauth2client")]


# ------------------------------------------------- F10 contract test
def test_f10_credential_format_and_scopes_contract(tmp_path, lieer_repo, fake_gmail_server):
    """F10: the Vault secret's credential carries the scopes the service
    requires (REQUIRED_SCOPES, service-owned; lieer 1.6 requests the same
    three), the service's copy is byte-identical, and real gmi accepts a
    valid google-auth blob."""
    secret = REDACTED / "secret"
    secret.write_text(dummy_credential_json())
    acct_dir = tmp_path / "Mail" / "a"
    acct_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
    mgr = CredentialManager("a", secret, acct_dir)
    mgr.sync()
    blob = json.loads((acct_dir / ".credentials.gmailieer.json").read_text())
    assert {"token", "refresh_token", "client_id", "client_secret", "expiry", "scopes"} <= blob.keys()
    assert set(REQUIRED_SCOPES) <= set(blob["scopes"])
    assert (acct_dir / ".credentials.gmailieer.json").read_text() == secret.read_text()
    assert mgr.load().refresh_token == REDACTED"refresh_token"]

    # real lieer accepts a (valid, unexpired) credential as-is
    fake_gmail_server.backend.insert_message("f10", label_ids=["INBOX"], raw=make_raw_message("f10"))
    cred = lieer_repo.root / ".credentials.gmailieer.json"
    cred.write_text(dummy_credential_json())
    os.chmod(cred, 0o600)
    result = run_pull(lieer_repo.root, env=lieer_repo.env, timeout=60, gmi_path=_gmi())
    assert result.outcome is PullOutcome.OK, (result.stdout, result.stderr)


def test_dummy_credential_blob_is_google_auth_and_far_future():
    """The shared dummy blob is a google-auth authorized-user credential
    (so lieer 1.6 never refreshes it) with a far-future expiry."""
    from gmailsync.dummy_credentials import dummy_credential

    blob = dummy_credential()
    assert set(blob) == {"token", "refresh_token", "client_id", "client_secret", "token_uri", "scopes", "expiry"}
    assert set(blob["scopes"]) == set(REQUIRED_SCOPES)
    assert datetime.strptime(blob["expiry"], "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ").year >= 2099

cd /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab/.worktrees/tc-8alf0.13/communication/email/gmail-sync && mkdir -p debug && cat > debug/mailread-offline-pod.yaml <<'EOF'
---
# Short-lived debug pod behind `just mail-* --offline` (design §6.12, D26).
# Used when the mail store service pod is down or crash-looping: it mounts the
# data PVC READ-ONLY (RWO allows it on the single kprod node) and runs the same
# read-only notmuch commands (python -m gmailsync.mailread) via kubectl exec.
# NOT part of the kustomization: scripts/mail-exec.sh renders and applies it
# per invocation (__POD_NAME__ is substituted) and deletes it afterwards. It
# never runs while a restore is in progress (the script refuses when
# /data/state/restore-in-progress exists).
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: __POD_NAME__
  namespace: communication--email--gmail-sync
  labels:
    app: gmail-sync-mailread-offline
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 1800
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        nodeSelectorTerms:
          - matchExpressions:
              - key: kubernetes.io/hostname
                operator: In
                values:
                  - kprod0
  containers:
    - name: mailread
      # the service image: same notmuch + gmailsync package as the live pod
      image: zot.twistcone.us/twistcone/gmail-sync:prod
      command: ["sleep", "1800"]
      securityContext:
        readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
          readOnly: true
      resources:
        requests:
          memory: "64Mi"
          cpu: "50m"
        limits:
          memory: "512Mi"
          cpu: "500m"
  volumes:
    - name: data
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: gmail-sync-data
        readOnly: true
EOF
cat > scripts/mail-exec.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run one read-only gmailsync command (mailread / ack_missing_content) against
# the mail store (design §6.12, D26).
#
#   mail-exec.sh <module> [--offline] <args...>
#
# Online (default): kubectl exec into the service pod. --offline: start a
# short-lived debug pod that mounts the data PVC read-only (for a down or
# crash-looping service pod), run the same command in it, delete the pod.
# --offline is read-only by construction and is refused while a restore is in
# progress (marker file /data/state/restore-in-progress). Never calls Gmail.
#
# Env: NAMESPACE, KUBE_CONTEXT (default kprod), MAILSTORE_TARGET (online target,
# default deploy/gmail-sync-mailstore), KUBECTL (test seam), POD_TEMPLATE.
set -euo pipefail

MODULE="${1:?usage: mail-exec.sh <module> [--offline] <args...>}"
shift
OFFLINE=0
ARGS=()
for a in "$@"; do
  if [[ $a == "--offline" ]]; then OFFLINE=1; else ARGS+=("$a"); fi
done

KUBECTL="${KUBECTL:-kubectl}"
CONTEXT="${KUBE_CONTEXT:-kprod}"
NS="${NAMESPACE:-communication--email--gmail-sync}"
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
TEMPLATE="${POD_TEMPLATE:-$HERE/../debug/mailread-offline-pod.yaml}"

if [[ $OFFLINE -eq 0 ]]; then
  exec "$KUBECTL" --context="$CONTEXT" -n "$NS" exec "${MAILSTORE_TARGET:-deploy/gmail-sync-mailstore}" -- \
    python -m "gmailsync.$MODULE" "${ARGS[@]}"
fi

POD="gmail-sync-mailread-$(date +%s)-$$"
cleanup() { "$KUBECTL" --context="$CONTEXT" -n "$NS" delete pod "$POD" --ignore-not-found --wait=false >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT
sed "s/__POD_NAME__/$POD/" "$TEMPLATE" | "$KUBECTL" --context="$CONTEXT" -n "$NS" apply -f - >&2
"$KUBECTL" --context="$CONTEXT" -n "$NS" wait --for=condition=Ready "pod/$POD" --timeout=180s >&2
if "$KUBECTL" --context="$CONTEXT" -n "$NS" exec "$POD" -- test -e /data/state/restore-in-progress; then
  echo "refusing --offline: a restore is in progress (/data/state/restore-in-progress)" >&2
  exit 3
fi
"$KUBECTL" --context="$CONTEXT" -n "$NS" exec "$POD" -- python -m "gmailsync.$MODULE" "${ARGS[@]}"
EOF
chmod +x scripts/mail-exec.sh

tool_input.command:
mkdir -p /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab/.worktrees/tc-rscq.3/infrastructure/vms/beads0/scripts /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab/.worktrees/tc-rscq.3/infrastructure/vms/beads0/tests && cd /home/tcadmin/workspace/homelab/.worktrees/tc-rscq.3/infrastructure/vms/beads0/scripts && cat > beads-backup.sh <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# beads-backup.sh -- nightly logical backup of the `tc` Dolt database on the
# beads0 guest (tc-rscq plan v5 D5): mysqldump -> gzip -> S3, then a
# node_exporter textfile freshness metric. Packaged by
# infrastructure/vms/beads0/configuration.nix (writeShellApplication) and run
# by beads0-backup.service; infrastructure/vms/beads0/tests/beads-backup.bats
# exercises this exact file with `mysqldump` and `aws` PATH shims.
#
# It ports the dump + upload of agents/beads-server/base/backup-cronjob.yaml
# (same flags, same truncation guard, same verify-before-delete), merged into
# one script because there is no initContainer/container split on a VM.
#
# Every flag on the mysqldump line is load-bearing against Dolt specifically:
#   --ssl-mode=DISABLED     the sql-server has no TLS.
#   no --single-transaction Dolt has no SAVEPOINT.
#   --column-statistics=0   drops the ANALYZE ... HISTOGRAM trailer Dolt cannot
#                           parse on restore.
#   --skip-lock-tables      Dolt does not implement LOCK TABLES.
#   --no-tablespaces        InnoDB tablespace queries are N/A.
# Oracle's mysqldump is required (MariaDB's opens with SET @@MAX_STATEMENT_TIME,
# which Dolt rejects). `dolt dump` cannot be used (no remote-context support).
#
# The metric is written ONLY after the upload is confirmed, so a failed dump,
# truncated dump or unconfirmed upload never advances the staleness alert.
#
# Env (all overridable; defaults are the production values):
#   BACKUP_DIR           local scratch, on /persist (root is a 1 GiB tmpfs)
#   DOLT_HOST/DOLT_PORT/DOLT_USER
#   DOLT_PASSWORD_FILE   Vault-rendered password, read into MYSQL_PWD (kept off
#                        argv) unless MYSQL_PWD is already set
#   S3_BUCKET/S3_PREFIX/S3_ENDPOINT   S3_PREFIX must end in "/"; Phase 1 uses a
#                        staging prefix distinct from the k8s CronJob's beads/
#   METRIC_PERSIST_FILE  metric copy that survives reboots (root is tmpfs)
#   METRIC_TEXTFILE      node_exporter textfile collector destination
#   AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY  from the unit's EnvironmentFile
set -euo pipefail

BACKUP_DIR="${BACKUP_DIR:-/persist/beads-backup}"
DOLT_HOST="${DOLT_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
DOLT_PORT="${DOLT_PORT:-3307}"
DOLT_USER="${DOLT_USER:-beads}"
DOLT_PASSWORD_FILE="${DOLT_PASSWORD_FILE:-/run/secrets/beads-dolt-password}"
S3_BUCKET="${S3_BUCKET:-kagents-beads}"
S3_PREFIX="${S3_PREFIX:-beads0-staging/}"
S3_ENDPOINT="${S3_ENDPOINT:-http://synfra.twistcone.us:8333}"
METRIC_PERSIST_FILE="${METRIC_PERSIST_FILE:-/persist/node_exporter/beads0_backup.prom}"
METRIC_TEXTFILE="${METRIC_TEXTFILE:-/var/lib/node_exporter/textfile_collector/beads0_backup.prom}"

if [ -z "${MYSQL_PWD:-}" ]; then
  if [ ! -r "${DOLT_PASSWORD_FILE}" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: MYSQL_PWD unset and ${DOLT_PASSWORD_FILE} is not readable" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  MYSQL_PWD="$(cat "${DOLT_PASSWORD_FILE}")"
fi
export MYSQL_PWD

case "${S3_PREFIX}" in
  */) ;;
  *)
    echo "ERROR: S3_PREFIX must end in '/', got '${S3_PREFIX}'" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

mkdir -p "${BACKUP_DIR}"
STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
NAME="tc_${STAMP}.sql.gz"
DUMP="${BACKUP_DIR}/${NAME}"
PARTIAL="${DUMP}.partial"
S3_URL="s3://${S3_BUCKET}/${S3_PREFIX}${NAME}"

# A previous failed run may have left scratch behind; never upload it.
rm -f "${BACKUP_DIR}"/*.partial

echo "=== Starting beads0 (tc) backup: ${DUMP} ==="

mysqldump \
  --host="${DOLT_HOST}" --port="${DOLT_PORT}" --user="${DOLT_USER}" \
  --ssl-mode=DISABLED \
  --skip-lock-tables \
  --no-tablespaces \
  --set-gtid-purged=OFF \
  --column-statistics=0 \
  --databases tc | gzip >"${PARTIAL}"

# A truncated dump is worse than no dump: it would still advance the freshness
# metric and silence the staleness alert. Publish only once mysqldump's own
# end-of-dump trailer is present (pipefail above already fails the run if
# mysqldump itself errors).
LAST_LINE="$(gzip -dc "${PARTIAL}" | tail -n 1)"
case "${LAST_LINE}" in
  "-- Dump completed"*) ;;
  *)
    echo "ERROR: dump is truncated; last line was: ${LAST_LINE}" >&2
    rm -f "${PARTIAL}"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac
mv "${PARTIAL}" "${DUMP}"
echo "Backup written: ${DUMP}"

echo "--- S3 upload ---"
aws s3 cp "${DUMP}" "${S3_URL}" --endpoint-url="${S3_ENDPOINT}"

# Confirm the object landed before trusting it. Do NOT delete the local copy or
# touch the metric on an unconfirmed upload.
if ! aws s3 ls "${S3_URL}" --endpoint-url="${S3_ENDPOINT}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: s3 ls did not confirm upload of ${S3_URL} -- leaving local copy at ${DUMP}" >&2
  exit 1
fi
echo "Confirmed: ${S3_URL}"

# Retention against the S3 copy is the sibling beads0-s3-prune service; the
# local scratch copy is no longer needed.
rm -f "${DUMP}"

# Freshness metric (git0 pattern): written to /persist first, then installed
# into the textfile collector. Root is tmpfs, so beads0-backup-metric-restore
# re-installs the /persist copy at boot.
mkdir -p "$(dirname "${METRIC_PERSIST_FILE}")" "$(dirname "${METRIC_TEXTFILE}")"
tmp="${METRIC_PERSIST_FILE}.tmp"
cat >"${tmp}" <<METRIC
# HELP backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds Unix time of the last successful backup.
# TYPE backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds gauge
backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds{job="beads0"} $(date +%s)
METRIC
mv -f "${tmp}" "${METRIC_PERSIST_FILE}"
install -m0644 "${METRIC_PERSIST_FILE}" "${METRIC_TEXTFILE}"

echo ""
echo "=== Backup complete ==="
EOF
chmod +x beads-backup.sh; shellcheck beads-backup.sh && echo ok
